analysis.subject: civics
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains presidential election timing and the typical election cycle from candidate registration and announcements through primary debates primaries and caucuses nominating conventions debates election day electoral college and inauguration.

overview.headline: Steps of the United States presidential election cycle

keyPoints.point: Presidential election occurs every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November
keyPoints.quote: An election for president of the United States happens every four years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November.

keyPoints.point: Presidential election cycle spans almost two years from candidate registration to inauguration
keyPoints.quote: The process of electing a president takes almost two years.

keyPoints.point: Candidates register with Federal Election Commission and later announce intentions before primaries
keyPoints.quote: Candidates register with the Federal Election Commission to run for president.

keyPoints.point: Electors cast their votes in December and Congress counts electoral votes in early January before inauguration
keyPoints.quote: Electors cast their votes for president in the Electoral College.
